Hi Marissa / team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. As we discussed, the priorities for the first two weeks are: dashboards for campus-prod latency, tracing hooks for our auth and billing services, and an initial alert matrix that maps to our on-call tiers.

A couple of constraints from our side: our security team wants the trace headers to avoid sending PIIs, and our SRE lead prefers alerts to be routed to PagerDuty with a low-noise policy for anything below 10% error-rate spikes.

Can you share a proposed runbook skeleton and an action-owner table so our on-call can start rehearsals? We have a compliance review scheduled for Oct 10th and would like to show a concrete plan.

Thanks,
Emma

Emma — thanks for the clear priorities. Attaching a first-pass runbook (OBS-runbook-v0.3.md) and a small alert matrix CSV that maps signals to PagerDuty tiers. High-level plan below.

Summary plan (first 10 business days):
- Day 1–3: Finalize signal definitions and error taxonomy with BlueBridge (ownership: Marissa)
- Day 4–6: Instrument tracing hooks (Ben) — auth + billing SDK hooks, sample header format (no PIIs)
- Day 7–9: Dashboard assembly and validation with product scenes (Laura)
- Day 10: Runbook dry run + on-call handoff meeting (Marissa, BlueBridge SRE)

Key implementation notes:
- We will use Redwood's prefix caching for auth flows to keep tokenization cost low; no PII will be embedded in traces — we will instead include stable request IDs and hashed user ids.
- Alert routing: tier-1 (pg duty: oncall-sre) for service-affecting errors; tier-2 (email + slack) for degradation signals. The attached alert-matrix.csv includes thresholds we recommend; happy to adjust after your SRE reviews.

Next steps: please confirm a deployment window for the tracing change (we suggest a staged rollout to one region first), and let us know who from your SRE will attend the runbook dry run on Oct 11th.

Attachments: OBS-runbook-v0.3.md (runbook skeleton), alert-matrix.csv (thresholds)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Observability onboarding: runbook draft & on-call routing blueprint

Emma / team — quick technical notes from the instrumentation side:

1) Tracing hooks
- We'll provide lightweight SDK snippets for Java (Spring), Node (Express) and Python (FastAPI).
- Trace header format: X-RW-Trace: <trace-id>;<span-id>;<flags>. No user-specific fields. For correlation we'll include an "x-request-hash" (SHA256 of user id + salt) if you want aggregated user metrics without revealing identity.

2) Dashboards
- Laura will onboard your product scenes into a dashboard proto; we'll start with an APM-style latency heatmap for auth flows and a funnel view for billing (success/fail by step).

3) Alert noise suppression
- We'll implement a sliding-window aggregation and a minimum 5-minute burn-in to avoid flapping. For your 10% spike policy we recommend alerting on sustained >10% error-rate for 5 minutes and >25% for 1 minute as urgency escalation.

I'll drop a small diagram and the SDK links into the shared Drive and tag OPS-427 in Jira for tracking.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
